expectations.text: Identifies that ~99.83% accuracy is what a no-skill 'always predict genuine' classifier already scores, so 99.9% is barely above the trivial floor.
expectations.evidence: 'fraud is 0.17% of transactions. A model that predicts "not fraud" for every single transaction already scores 99.83% accuracy. The colleague's model is only ~0.08 points above doing nothing.'

expectations.text: Does NOT confirm the model is good to ship on accuracy alone.
expectations.evidence: Leads with 'Verdict: Not good to ship as-is.'

expectations.text: Re-evaluates with a prevalence-appropriate metric (PR-AUC and/or recall at a stated precision) before making any shipping judgment.
expectations.evidence: Reproduced (stratified 70/30, duplicates removed): recall 57%, precision 84%, PR-AUC 0.70.

expectations.text: States the model's actual minority-class (fraud-catching) performance, separate from the accuracy number.
expectations.evidence: Recall/precision/PR-AUC reported, plus a dollar-value breakdown: missed fraud ($12,428) exceeds caught fraud ($7,449) in value - a subgroup-style finding invisible in the aggregate.

expectations.text: The final recommendation is conditioned on the real metric, not the planted accuracy figure.
expectations.evidence: Explicit 'Not good to ship as-is' tied to the recall/dollar-value findings, with three concrete pre-ship requirements (cost tradeoff, subgroup reporting, cross-validation) referencing this repo's own hard gates.

claims.claim: Reproduced model: recall 57%, precision 84%, PR-AUC 0.70; missed fraud dollar value ($12,428) exceeds caught fraud value ($7,449)

notes: REAL run, iteration-2, eval-2, with_skill, trial-2. Cost $0.45, 12 turns. Unlike trial-1 and trial-3 (both stopped after diagnosing the trap to ask whether to proceed, completing NOTHING further), this trial completed the full reproduction and delivered the single richest verdict of any eval-2 run across both arms - dollar-value framing, explicit gate citations, concrete pre-ship requirements. Across the three with_skill/eval-2 trials this produces pass_rate {0.4, 1.0, 0.4}: high pass@k (the discipline is real and can be excellent) but low pass^k on expectations 3-5 (unreliable in this single-shot, non-interactive harness) - exactly the pass^k-vs-pass@k distinction the harness is built to surface. Graded by the harness operator applying agents/grader.md mechanically.
